en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Chapter on Mindfulness, 1.
The Question on Cherishing the Body.
The king said:
“Venerable Nāgasena, is the body dear to those who have gone forth?
“Indeed not, great king, is the body dear to those who have gone forth.”
“But why then, Bhante, do you cherish and dote over me?
“What then, Great King, has an arrow ever struck you when you have gone into battle?
“Yes, Bhante, it has.”
“Great King, why is it that this wound is smeared with ointment, anointed with oil, and bandaged with a fine cloth?
“Yes, venerable sir, it is smeared with ointment, anointed with oil, and bandaged with a fine cloth.
“But Great King, is this wound dear to you, such that it is smeared with ointment, anointed with oil, and bandaged with a fine cloth?”
“Venerable sir, the wound is not dear to me; nevertheless, it is smeared with an ointment for the purpose of healing the flesh, anointed with oil, and bandaged with a fine cloth strip.
“In the same way, great king, the body is not dear to those who have gone forth. Yet, without clinging, renunciants maintain the body for the sake of supporting the holy life.
Furthermore, great king, the Blessed One has said that the body is like a wound; therefore, renunciants maintain the body like a wound, without clinging.”
This was also said, Great King, by the Blessed One:
“Covered with moist skin,
a great wound with nine openings;”
"It flows out on all sides,
with the stench of impure putridity.
"Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!"
The first question on being fond of the body.
